# vLLM 0.25.1 decode-marginal throughput, MEASURED on this RTX 3060 (2026-07-20)
# f16, CUDA graphs ON (enforce_eager=False), prefill cancelled via 2-point gen-length subtraction.
# Reproduce: BATCH=<n> ~/.local/share/goai-vllm/vllm-venv/bin/python testdata/vllm_ctx_sweep.py
# batch  ctx128   ctx256   ctx384   ctx512   (tok/s)
   64    5096.2   5020.1   4915.8   4367.2
  256    7465.9   6630.7   6910.7   6119.6
  512    8720.5   7711.1   6730.7   6048.4
#
# GoAI full-step (graph-gqa-f16-full, 22L, same GPU/session) for comparison:
# batch  ctx128   ctx256   ctx512
#   64   5503     4728     3621
#  256   8019     -        -
#  512   8675     -        -
#  768   8790     -        -
# => ctx128: GoAI 1.08x@64, 1.07x@256, 0.99x@512 (parity).  ctx512@64: vLLM 1.21x (FlashDecoding).

# ACCUMULATE-PRECISION RESOLUTION (2026-07-20): GoAI decode GEMMs auto-enable f16-accumulate
# (CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F) on GeForce, exploiting consumer-Ampere's 2x f16-acc tensor rate. vLLM
# defaults to f32-accumulate. MATCHED-precision (both f32-acc) full-step decode, ctx128:
# batch  GoAI-f32acc  GoAI-f16acc  vLLM(f32acc)   matched-ratio
#   64    4571         5503         5096           vLLM 1.11x
#  256    6219         8019         7466           vLLM 1.20x
#  512    6643         8675         8721           vLLM 1.31x
# => At MATCHED precision vLLM's decode kernels are 1.1-1.4x faster. GoAI's f16-acc trade
#    (validated token-identical on TinyLlama) closes it to 1.07-1.08x vs vLLM's f32-acc default,
#    but that is not a like-for-like kernel comparison. Force GoAI f32-acc: GOAI_CUDA_F16ACC=0.
